item.title: Metastable states are precursors of Turing patterns in Adaptive Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.28828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In networked reaction-diffusion systems, emergence of patterns from a homogeneous equilibrium can be described by Turing instability. Recently, Turing theory has been developed to include adaptive networks where, i.e., link weights change as a function of the states of the nodes. In this work we show that metastable states, defined as long living transient epochs with unique dynamical properties, could be observed in a range of parameters between Turing patterns and absence of any spatial pattern. Stated differently in the metastable regime the system ''switches'' between the homogeneous solution and the Turing pattern, never settling in any of those states, i.e., alternating silent and spiking regimes. By using phase diagrams and recurrence plots, we have numerically shown the existence of metastable states for the Brusselator model. Moreover, the dependence of the emergence of the metastable states on the adaptive control parameter has been characterized. The applicability of methods and ideas proposed in this work go beyond the considered case, they can help us in understanding conditions under which metastable states arise and could thus be informative to predict and control the latter.
item.dc:creator: S. Nirmala Jenifer, Timoteo Carletti

item.title: Generalized Emergence through Coarse-Graining: A Category-Theoretic Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.29302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantitative theories of emergence use diverse representations and indicators, making their shared structure difficult to identify. This paper develops a category-theoretic framework for generalized emergence through coarse-graining, without presupposing dynamics, probability, interventions, or specific information measures. System descriptions are represented by categories and coarse-grainings by functors. Generalized emergence requires improvement of a specified description attribute along an admissible, nontrivial functor; an extension evaluates corresponding internal morphisms. The criterion separates structural admissibility from attribute improvement and accommodates several attributes under a chosen comparison order. Different functors embody different observational perspectives, making emergence observer-dependent. Selecting an optimal coarse-graining can partially reduce this dependence, but only under a given attribute and constraints; optimality guarantees neither uniqueness nor emergence. For dynamical models, state and dynamical coarse-graining are defined separately and linked by strict or approximate closure; unification by one functor is a special case. Computational mechanics, causal emergence, and approximate dynamical reversibility illustrate the dynamical case. Two static examples show the criterion at work: symmetry emergence, where coarse-graining polygons improves rotational and dihedral symmetry, and cohesion emergence, where coarse-graining networks raises global efficiency, edge density, and clustering. Each example also contains an equally coarse case that does not qualify: for polygons, one of the two symmetry measures improves while the other worsens, and for networks, all three cohesion attributes decline.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwei Liu, Jiang Zhang

item.title: Realizability and tunability of synchronized optical soliton collision patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.29357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronizing the positions and phases of colliding optical solitons can maximize the amplitude at the collision center, producing a large-amplitude localized wave. We investigate whether multiple prescribed synchronized collisions can be jointly realized within a single multisoliton field and to what extent their relative retarded times and propagation distances can be varied continuously while preserving synchronization. Ideal optical fiber propagation is modeled here by the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with zero boundary conditions. For distinct discrete eigenvalues, we derive an affine system of equations constraining the collision event positions to determine whether the synchronization conditions at different events can be satisfied simultaneously. Furthermore, for a fixed discrete spectrum and a realizable complete collision organization in which each soliton pair participates in exactly one event, continuous tuning of the relative event positions while preserving synchronization requires collinearity of the auxiliary spectral points constructed from the discrete eigenvalues. When these points are noncollinear, only uniform translations of all event centers are possible. Any three-soliton spectrum with distinct soliton velocities and noncollinear auxiliary spectral points supports both a collective collision and a rigid fully pairwise collision organization. A physically admissible four-soliton family with collinear auxiliary spectral points demonstrates continuous internal tunability.
item.dc:creator: Bo-Jie Deng, Rui Guo, Jia-Xue Niu, Jian-Wen Zhang

item.title: Weakly Nonlinear Whitham Modulation and Dispersive Shock Waves in the Modified Gardner Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate weakly nonlinear Whitham modulation and dispersive shock waves (DSWs) in a modified Gardner equation. A three-equation modulation system is derived through a Stokes expansion and averaged conservation laws. Perturbative analysis of its characteristic structure provides explicit conditions for hyperbolicity and genuine nonlinearity, and identifies a wavenumber-dependent transition between real and complex characteristic splitting. The dispersive resolution of compressive Riemann data is examined using DSW fitting, yielding analytical predictions for the harmonic- and solitary-wave edge velocities. The solitary-wave prediction is further supported by a traveling-wave energy analysis. Numerical continuation of the modulation characteristics identifies the limitations of the weakly nonlinear approximation, while direct numerical simulations using a Fourier pseudospectral method confirm close agreement with the predicted leading-edge velocity and the leading solitary-wave amplitude for the resolved cases. These results clarify the weakly nonlinear characteristic structure and the edge dynamics of dispersive shocks for the modified Gardner equation.
item.dc:creator: Nese Ozdemir, Ali Demirci, Ayse Peker Dobie

item.title: Fifth-order KdV solitary waves in a nonlinear electrical transmission line
item.description: arXiv:2611.31074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the controlled experimental observation of solitary waves governed by the fifth-order dispersion Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To achieve vanishing cubic dispersion, we use a mutual inductive coupling between nearest-neighbor inductors within a nonlinear electrical transmission line. We then experimentally characterize the resulting solitary waves through direct spatiotemporal measurements of the dispersion relation, its oscillatory tail profiles, amplitude-width scaling, and amplitude-velocity relation, finding good agreement with semi-analytical predictions. Collision experiments between two (co- or counter-propagating) solitary waves also show that their self-similar profile persists after interaction, up to a time shift. Dissipation effects are also quantified.
item.dc:creator: Loic Fache, Filip Novkoski, Eric Falcon

item.title: Higher-Order Modulational Instability in Spin-Orbit-Coupled Bose-Einstein Condensates: Finite-Raman Effects and Branch-Resolved Spectral Redistribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.28514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate higher-order modulational instability and the nonlinear spectral redistribution in a spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) binary Bose--Einstein condensate with equal interactions. For finite Raman coupling, the system is nonintegrable and exhibits both nonoscillatory and oscillatory instability regimes. Raman coupling reshapes the instability bands and changes what harmonics can grow. Direct simulations show that this reorganization modifies the subsequent nonlinear sideband dynamics. In the zero-Raman limit, SOC shifts successive harmonics between instability bands and stability gaps at a fixed carrier wavenumber. It thereby controls higher-order instability, distinct breather branches, and frequency-hopping sequences. We derive exact algebraic coefficients for the carrier and arbitrary-order sidebands. This yields an exact geometric power spectrum for the complete infinite sideband sequence and a unified description of carrier depletion, directional imbalance, and sideband decay, including an exact relation between the instability gain and the minimum spectral decay rate. For two coexisting breather branches with the same background and modulation wavenumber, the higher-gain branch can have a smaller maximum carrier depletion, a slower high-order spectral decay, and a weaker directional imbalance. SOC can also restore a symmetric sideband spectrum when the SOC-induced momentum shift compensates the carrier wavenumber, even when both $k$ and $k_L$ are nonzero. These analytical and numerical results clarify how SOC and Raman couplings organize higher-order instability and nonlinear spectral redistribution, providing a unified framework for studying coherent nonlinear-wave dynamics in multicomponent condensates.
item.dc:creator: Cui-Cui Ding, Boris A. Malomed, Qin Zhou

item.title: Dark and bright solitons in a multimodal lithium tantalate microresonator
item.description: arXiv:2611.30313v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bright-soliton and dark-pulse microcombs provide complementary outputs. Integrating both states in a single resonator would expand the operating capabilities of an integrated coherent source, but requires opposite group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) channels while reconciling localized interfamily interaction for dark-pulse formation with spectral isolation for independent bright-soliton pumping. Wavelength-addressed access to both states is achieved in a LiTaO$_3$ microring through two TE-like transverse mode families. The higher-order TE$_{10}$ family fulfills two distinct roles in different spectral regions. Within localized avoided-mode-crossing regions, mode-resolved spectroscopy implicates TE$_{10}$ in perturbing the normal-GVD TE$_{00}$ resonance sequence. Away from these regions, TE$_{10}$ retains anomalous GVD and remains spectrally isolated as an independently pumpable bright-soliton channel; at representative pump resonances, the closest resonance of the non-addressed family is separated by 75--192 loaded cavity linewidths. With the input polarization held fixed, pumping TE$_{00}$ and TE$_{10}$ resonances generates dark-pulse and bright-soliton microcombs, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental realization of a dark-pulse microcomb in an integrated LiTaO$_3$ microring. These results establish transverse-mode-family engineering as a route to combining localized modal interaction with independent spectral addressing in a single microresonator.
item.dc:creator: Huizong Zhu, Yuyao Guo, Xiangfei Cheng, Yiqun Wu, Juanjuan Lu

item.title: Beyond the Blueprint: The Continuing Evolution of Turing's Theory of Morphogenesis
item.description: arXiv:2611.30543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Turing's article ``The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis'' has profoundly influenced conceptual views on the emergence of biological form across scales and species. It has also served as a foundational framework to guide experimental investigations into the mechanisms that underlie pattern formation. In this article, we trace the historical development of Turing's ideas and examine their integration into contemporary research programs. We critically assess the broad and often overlapping concepts that have derived from Turing's work, both highlighting value in productive applications of the theory and suggesting that skepticism should remain in overly simplistic validations. By clarifying these concepts and their intrinsic limitations, we rethink contemporary approaches aimed at understanding the essential principles that govern biological pattern formation. We pose some important challenges that will require interdisciplinary expertise to overcome, and which will necessitate fundamentally new paradigms to understand the physical origin of Darwin's ``endless forms most beautiful''.
item.dc:creator: Andrew L. Krause, Kevin J. Painter, Denis J. Headon

item.title: Motion of dissipative solitons in quasi-one-dimensional potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.30594v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the motion of two-dimensional (2D) dissipative solitons and soliton pairs in the framework of the cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation with quasi-1D potentials, spatially periodic or radial-lattice ones. The equation is solved numerically for inputs representing one or two fundamental solitons, which are set in motion by a kick. For the quasi-1D potential, the kick parallel to the potential axis naturally initiates free motion of the 2D solitons, as the model remains Galilean-invariant in this direction. Motion in the transverse direction, which may entail pulse multiplication, commences if the kick is strong enough. Oblique kicks lead to a straightforward superposition of the longitudinal and transverse motions. Also considered is the collision between 2D solitons moving in the longitudinal and diagonal directions. In the radial potential, the soliton kicked towards the center may bounce back from the central potential hill or pass it, producing complex trajectories and splitting of the moving soliton.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Besse, Herv{\'e} Leblond, Dumitru Mihalache, Boris A. Malomed

item.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
item.description: arXiv:2608.11370v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.
item.dc:creator: Manuel A. Mart\'inez S\'anchez, Christoph Adam, Danial Saadatmand
